content.text:
I ran `npm test`. 7 of 10 tests pass and 3 fail. In each failure the service code is wrong, not the test. I haven't changed anything.

| Test | File | Expected | Actual | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `findByEmail ignores soft-deleted users` | `tests/auth-service.test.js:5` | `null` | Alan's user row | `src/services/auth-service.js:5` only checks `u.email === email` and never checks `u.deleted_at === null`, so soft-deleted users are still returned. |
| `totalPaidCents counts only paid orders` | `tests/order-service.test.js:14` | `14600` (4200 + 9900 + 500) | `1350` | `src/services/order-service.js:9` matches `o.status === 'quote'` when it should match `'paid'`, so it adds up the one quote order instead of the paid ones. |
| `uncapturedTotalCents sums uncaptured payments` | `tests/payment-service.test.js:14` | `9900` | `4200` | `src/services/payment-service.js:10` matches `p.captured === true` when it should match `false`, so it adds up the captured payment. |

**Why the error output looks nested:** in `src/db.js:33-37`, `query()` wraps the callback in a `try/catch`. When an assertion fails inside the callback, the catch calls the callback a second time with the assertion error as `err`. The test's `assert.equal(err, null)` then fails with the original error inside it. That's why each failure shows "expected `null`" wrapped around the real mismatch. The real values are in the inner error (e.g. `1350 !== 14600`). Any exception thrown inside a `query` callback will make the callback run twice.

**A gap the passing tests miss:** `isActive` is built on `findByEmail`, so it currently returns `true` for the soft-deleted user `alan@example.com`. Its only test checks a live user, so it still passes.

I ran `npm test`. 7 of 10 tests pass and 3 fail. In each failure the service code is wrong, not the test. I haven't changed anything.

| Test | File | Expected | Actual | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `findByEmail ignores soft-deleted users` | `tests/auth-service.test.js:5` | `null` | Alan's user row | `src/services/auth-service.js:5` only checks `u.email === email` and never checks `u.deleted_at === null`, so soft-deleted users are still returned. |
| `totalPaidCents counts only paid orders` | `tests/order-service.test.js:14` | `14600` (4200 + 9900 + 500) | `1350` | `src/services/order-service.js:9` matches `o.status === 'quote'` when it should match `'paid'`, so it adds up the one quote order instead of the paid ones. |
| `uncapturedTotalCents sums uncaptured payments` | `tests/payment-service.test.js:14` | `9900` | `4200` | `src/services/payment-service.js:10` matches `p.captured === true` when it should match `false`, so it adds up the captured payment. |

**Why the error output looks nested:** in `src/db.js:33-37`, `query()` wraps the callback in a `try/catch`. When an assertion fails inside the callback, the catch calls the callback a second time with the assertion error as `err`. The test's `assert.equal(err, null)` then fails with the original error inside it. That's why each failure shows "expected `null`" wrapped around the real mismatch. The real values are in the inner error (e.g. `1350 !== 14600`). Any exception thrown inside a `query` callback will make the callback run twice.

**A gap the passing tests miss:** `isActive` is built on `findByEmail`, so it currently returns `true` for the soft-deleted user `alan@example.com`. Its only test checks a live user, so it still passes.
